accommodations.name: Victoria Falls Safari Lodge
accommodations.location: Victoria Falls National Park border, Zimbabwe
accommodations.tagline: Perched high on a natural plateau overlooking an active wildlife waterhole.
accommodations.shortDescription: A wildlife-oriented lodge overlooking bushveld and a waterhole on the Victoria Falls Safari Collection estate.
accommodations.editorialOverview: A wildlife-oriented lodge overlooking bushveld and a waterhole on the Victoria Falls Safari Collection estate. The lodge includes a two-tiered swimming pool, MaKuwa-Kuwa Restaurant, Buffalo Bar and complimentary scheduled town shuttle.
accommodations.whyWeRecommend: We recommend Victoria Falls Safari Lodge because it offers an authentic safari lodge feel without leaving town. Sitting on your private balcony with a cold drink watching wild elephants at the waterhole is one of the definitive Victoria Falls experiences. It is exceptional value for wildlife lovers and couples alike.

atAGlance.roomTypesSummary: 72 rooms (24 Standard, 42 Waterhole Facing, 6 Waterhole Facing Suites)

roomTypes.name: Lodge Standard Room
roomTypes.shortDescription: An air-conditioned lodge room with comfortable beds, mosquito nets and a private balcony.
roomTypes.description: The Lodge Standard Room offers a restful stay at Victoria Falls Safari Lodge, with a private balcony and access to the estate’s waterhole-viewing facilities. It includes air conditioning, ceiling fan, Wi-Fi, tea/coffee facilities and twin three-quarter beds that can be combined into a king. The minibar is stocked on request at guests’ cost, unlike the suite category.

roomTypes.name: Lodge Waterhole Facing Room
roomTypes.description: Choose the Lodge Waterhole Facing Room for its position overlooking the active waterhole at Victoria Falls Safari Lodge. Rooms include convertible twin-to-king beds, air conditioning, ceiling fans, mosquito nets, Wi-Fi and tea/coffee facilities. Wildlife sightings are possible but never guaranteed. Minibar supplies are on request at guests’ cost.
roomTypes.shortDescription: A comfortable lodge room with a balcony facing the wildlife waterhole and surrounding bush.

roomTypes.name: Lodge Waterhole Facing Suite
roomTypes.description: The Lodge Waterhole Facing Suite is the lodge’s premium category, with a view towards its wildlife waterhole and additional suite comforts. The hotel states that only its six Waterhole Facing Suites include bathtubs, and that a complimentary minibar is restocked each day with selected local beverages. Guests also have Wi-Fi, air conditioning and access to lodge dining and leisure facilities.
roomTypes.shortDescription: A more spacious waterhole-facing suite with a bathtub and daily complimentary minibar service.

locationInfo.address: Stand 471 Squire Cummings Avenue, Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe
locationInfo.departurePoints: Direct lobby pick-up for all guided tours & helicopter flights.

accommodations.name: Ilala Lodge Hotel
accommodations.tagline: The closest hotel to Victoria Falls, where mist rises over lush manicured lawns.
accommodations.shortDescription: A boutique hotel within walking distance of the rainforest entrance, set across Garden, Pool and Deluxe wings with Cassia Restaurant.
accommodations.editorialOverview: A boutique hotel within walking distance of the rainforest entrance, set across Garden, Pool and Deluxe wings. Guest facilities include gardens, swimming pool and Cassia Restaurant (the current name, replacing older Palm Restaurant references).
accommodations.whyWeRecommend: We love Ilala Lodge Hotel for travellers who prioritize convenience, walkability, and refined dining. You can easily walk to the entry gate of Victoria Falls, local markets, and cafes without needing taxis. The combination of boutique hospitality and prime proximity is unmatched.

atAGlance.pool: Sparkling outdoor pool with poolside bar

roomTypes.name: Classic Rooms
roomTypes.description: Classic Rooms at Ilala Lodge feature timber furnishings, an en-suite shower bathroom and a private patio or balcony overlooking the gardens and lawns. Guests may request king bedding or a twin configuration using two three-quarter beds. The hotel lists Wi-Fi, air conditioning, tea/coffee facilities, satellite TV and an in-room safe.
roomTypes.wing: Garden Wing / Pool Wing (exact wing by booking)
roomTypes.shortDescription: Teak-furnished rooms with a king or two three-quarter beds and a shower en-suite.

roomTypes.name: Deluxe Rooms
roomTypes.shortDescription: Refined rooms with garden-view patio or balcony and spacious shower bathrooms with double vanities.
roomTypes.description: The Deluxe Rooms are located in Ilala’s Deluxe Wing. Their 44 m² layout combines classic teak detailing and contemporary comforts, with either king bedding or two three-quarter twin beds. Each has a walk-in shower, double bathroom vanity and a private patio or balcony facing the gardens and surrounding natural landscape.

roomTypes.name: Classic Suites
roomTypes.description: Ilala’s Classic Suites are 75 m² and located on the upper level, with balconies towards the gardens and rising Falls spray. The sleeping layout includes a king bed and a separate three-quarter bed, making the suite useful for a small family. Selected arrangements can interconnect with a Classic Twin Room for larger families, subject to availability.
roomTypes.shortDescription: A suite with king and additional three-quarter beds, a balcony and optional interconnecting room.

roomTypes.name: Executive Suites
roomTypes.description: Ilala’s 104 m² Executive Suites offer a separate living room and bedroom, a king bed and a generous bathroom with walk-in shower, separate bathtub and twin basins. The balcony extends across the suite with views towards the Falls and surrounding vegetation. Added comforts include Wi-Fi and a complimentary minibar as described for the category.
roomTypes.shortDescription: Spacious suites with separate lounge, king bedroom and wraparound balcony facing the Falls direction.

roomTypes.name: Strathearn Suite
roomTypes.shortDescription: The hotel’s signature suite with lounge, kitchenette and an outdoor heated spa bath on the balcony.
roomTypes.description: The 128 m² Strathearn Suite is named after the hotel’s founder. It features a king bedroom, separate lounge and kitchenette, an indoor bathroom with bathtub, shower and double vanity, and a balcony with a heated spa bath looking towards the rising Falls spray. The hotel describes additional benefits such as in-room continental breakfast, sparkling wine and a river cruise subject to availability. Confirm which benefits apply to Outbound Holidays’ booked rate.

locationInfo.departurePoints: Walk to Falls entrance or lobby pick-up for excursions.

accommodations.name: Pioneers Victoria Falls
accommodations.location: Quiet Residential Suburbs, Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe
accommodations.tagline: A stylish, eco-conscious sanctuary nestled in tranquil landscaped gardens.
accommodations.shortDescription: A 50-room lodge on Mahogany Road, with landscaped gardens, two swimming pools, restaurant/lounge and spa.
accommodations.editorialOverview: A 50-room lodge on Mahogany Road, with landscaped gardens, two swimming pools, restaurant/lounge and spa. Its rooms have garden outlooks, air conditioning, tea/coffee amenities and double-vanity en-suite showers.
accommodations.whyWeRecommend: Pioneers is one of our top recommendations for travellers seeking high-end comfort and peace at an accessible price point. The gardens are impeccably maintained, the food is fresh and delicious, and the quiet setting ensures a restful night after action-packed safari days.

atAGlance.roomTypesSummary: 50 rooms overall (including 4 Family Rooms with Annex)

roomTypes.name: Standard / King or Twin Room
roomTypes.description: The lodge’s principal rooms feature tasteful classic furnishings and views of its gardens. They include a well-appointed en-suite shower bathroom with double vanity, mosquito nets, fans and air conditioning, room safe, hairdryer, tea and coffee facilities and Wi-Fi. King or twin bedding can be requested and the operator can advise on cots or extra beds for children.
roomTypes.shortDescription: Comfortable garden-facing accommodation with king or twin arrangements and modern en-suite facilities.

roomTypes.name: Family Room with Annex
roomTypes.description: Pioneers has four purpose-designed family rooms, each with a main room and an annex featuring twin beds decorated with children in mind. Guests have the standard lodge’s air conditioning, en-suite bathroom amenities and garden surroundings. Confirm the ages, sleeping arrangement, whether a cot is required and maximum occupancy before confirming the booking.
roomTypes.shortDescription: A family room with a main bedroom and connected twin-bedded children’s annex.

locationInfo.departurePoints: Complimentary lobby transfers organized for activities.

accommodations.name: Batonka Guest Lodge
accommodations.tagline: A tranquil haven of contemporary African elegance and personalized service.
accommodations.shortDescription: A garden-set 27-room lodge with indoor/outdoor dining, lounge, curio shop and pools.
accommodations.editorialOverview: A garden-set 27-room lodge with indoor/outdoor dining, lounge, curio shop and pools. Its main sellable categories are Garden View Rooms and Pool View Rooms; the Flame Lily Wing is an area within the existing Pool View inventory.
accommodations.whyWeRecommend: Batonka Guest Lodge is ideal for travellers wanting personalized, attentive service without the high-volume crowds of large resorts. The quiet residential location guarantees uninterrupted rest, while the lodge staff excel at arranging seamless daily excursions.

atAGlance.roomTypesSummary: 27 rooms (11 Garden View, 16 Pool View incl. 5 in Flame Lily Wing)

roomTypes.name: Garden View Room
roomTypes.description: Each Garden View Room has a spacious patio overlooking manicured lawns and trees visited by local birdlife. Batonka’s Garden View rooms include modern en-suite bathrooms with double basins and large shower, air conditioning, ceiling fan, king or twin arrangement on request, Wi-Fi, tea/coffee facilities and in-room safe. Eight of these rooms interlead, and one has a child-friendly annex, subject to room allocation.
roomTypes.shortDescription: A garden-facing room with private patio, double-vanity bathroom and walk-in shower.

roomTypes.name: Pool View Room
roomTypes.description: Batonka’s Pool View Rooms open to private patios facing landscaped lawns and a tranquil swimming pool. These rooms have an en-suite bathroom with double vanities, a bathtub and walk-in shower, air conditioning, Wi-Fi, in-room safe and tea/coffee station. Five of the 16 are located in the Flame Lily Wing, which has its own pool and shared leisure spaces.
roomTypes.wing: Pool View (some in Flame Lily Wing)
roomTypes.shortDescription: A comfortable pool-facing room with a private patio and bathroom offering both bath and shower.

locationInfo.departurePoints: Doorstep pickup for all river cruises and safari activities.

accommodations.name: The Victoria Falls Hotel
accommodations.tagline: The iconic 5-star "Grand Dame" established in 1904 with private access to the Falls.
accommodations.shortDescription: Colonial grandeur overlooking the Victoria Falls Bridge and Batoka Gorge. Enjoy high tea on the Stanley Terrace and walk directly to the rainforest entry.
accommodations.editorialOverview: Established in 1904, The Victoria Falls Hotel is a member of Leading Hotels of the World. Combining Edwardian elegance with modern luxury, the hotel offers direct views of the historic Victoria Falls Bridge and the rising mist of Mosi-oa-Tunya. Highlights include high tea served daily on the Stanley Terrace, fine dining at The Livingstone Room, and a private pathway directly to the rainforest park entry.
accommodations.whyWeRecommend: Unmatched history, world-class service, and iconic views make The Victoria Falls Hotel a bucket-list stay for luxury travellers and heritage enthusiasts.

roomTypes.name: Standard Rooms
roomTypes.shortDescription: A classic room category at The Victoria Falls Hotel, offering a base for exploring the Falls while enjoying the facilities of the historic five-star property.
roomTypes.description: Stay at one of Victoria Falls' best-known heritage hotels, established in 1904, with access to the property's gardens, restaurants and guest services. Standard Rooms are one of the hotel's official accommodation categories. The current accommodation listing does not provide enough room-specific detail to confirm their floor area, precise bed options, bathroom layout or individual views. Outbound Holidays can request the preferred bed configuration and confirm details with the hotel when preparing a quotation.

roomTypes.name: Classic Rooms
roomTypes.shortDescription: Comfortable 30 m² rooms with elegant furnishings, modern conveniences and shower-only bathrooms; selected rooms can interconnect for families.
roomTypes.description: Classic Rooms combine understated décor in grey and dark tones with timber furnishings and modern in-room comforts. Each room has a shower-only bathroom, tea and coffee-making facilities, a safe, minibar, air conditioning, IP television and USB charging points. Some rooms are interleading, making them useful for guests travelling as a family. The hotel also describes a component-room arrangement in which three Classic Rooms can operate under one key; this must be confirmed for the dates and group size requested.

roomTypes.name: Stables Signature Wing Rooms
roomTypes.description: The Stables Signature Wing is a separate section of The Victoria Falls Hotel with a more personalised arrival experience. Rooms combine contemporary furnishings with the property's heritage character and look towards the front lawns or landscaped courtyard. Each room has a bathroom with a bathtub and separate walk-in shower. Guests on eligible bookings can make use of the Stables lounge, private check-in, afternoon tea refreshments and other published benefits. The hotel's website excludes some of these benefits for upgrades and groups of five rooms or more, so their availability must be checked when quoting.
features: Views towards front lawns or courtyard (room-dependent)
roomTypes.shortDescription: Rooms in the hotel's exclusive Stables Signature Wing, overlooking the lawns or courtyard, with a dedicated lounge and private check-in.

roomTypes.name: Premium Rooms
roomTypes.description: The Premium Rooms offer a more spacious stay within The Victoria Falls Hotel, with an average floor area of 55 m² and a separate lounge area for relaxing. Rooms are found in different parts of the hotel and may overlook either the landscaped gardens or Batoka Gorge. They feature convertible king or twin bedding, an elegant bathroom with shower, air conditioning, IP television, a safe and tea and coffee-making facilities. The hotel also lists access to the Bulawayo Premium Lounge, a daily complimentary minibar and a welcome gift as Premium Room benefits. Early check-in may be available but is not guaranteed.
features: Wi-Fi, safe, IP TV & air conditioning
roomTypes.shortDescription: Spacious 55 m² rooms with a dedicated lounge area, flexible king or twin bedding and views of the gardens or Batoka Gorge, depending on room allocation.

roomTypes.name: Deluxe Suites
roomTypes.shortDescription: Elegant 70 m² suites with spacious living areas and bathrooms, offering views towards the Falls spray or Batoka Gorge.
roomTypes.description: Deluxe Suites provide additional space and comfort in the hotel's heritage surroundings. With an average area of 70 m², they have generous living space, spacious bathrooms with showers and king-size beds that can be converted where required. The hotel's official description highlights views of either the rising spray from Victoria Falls or Batoka Gorge. Guests are also offered access to the Bulawayo Premium Lounge and in-suite comforts including a minibar, safe, Wi-Fi, air conditioning, IP television and tea and coffee-making facilities. The specific view and bed arrangement should be confirmed when reserving.
features: View towards Falls spray or Batoka Gorge (suite-dependent)
Minibar, safe, Wi-Fi, IP TV & air conditioning

roomTypes.name: Executive Suites
roomTypes.shortDescription: Distinctive 70 m² heritage suites with separate lounges, walk-in wardrobes, bathtubs and showers, overlooking the hotel's gardens.
roomTypes.description: The hotel's three Executive Suites — Songwe, Baines and Jubilee — each have their own character inspired by Victorian and Edwardian style. Located within the North and South Hammerhead Wings, the suites average 70 m² and feature a private lounge separate from the bedroom, a walk-in wardrobe and a spacious bathroom with both a bathtub and separate shower. The hotel describes manicured garden views and special welcome touches such as flowers, fruit and chocolates. Additional comforts include a minibar, safe, Wi-Fi, air conditioning, IP television and tea and coffee-making facilities.
features: Wi-Fi, minibar, safe, IP TV & air conditioning

roomTypes.name: Royal Batoka Suite
roomTypes.shortDescription: An exclusive 121 m² two-bedroom suite with private living and dining spaces, a kitchenette and panoramic views towards Batoka Gorge and Victoria Falls Bridge.
roomTypes.description: Situated in the central section of The Victoria Falls Hotel, the Royal Batoka Suite combines classic Edwardian character with a spacious two-bedroom layout. The master bedroom has a king-size bed and en-suite bathroom with a freestanding bath and walk-in shower. The second bedroom offers a king or twin configuration and its own en-suite shower. A separate living room, dining room, guest toilet and kitchenette make the suite well suited to travellers seeking privacy and space to spend time together. The hotel's website highlights views of Batoka Gorge and the Victoria Falls Bridge. Butler service is described as available, but should be arranged and priced with the hotel.
features: Two bedrooms and two en-suite bathrooms
Master bedroom with freestanding bath & walk-in shower
Views of Batoka Gorge & Victoria Falls Bridge

roomTypes.name: Presidential Suite
roomTypes.shortDescription: A distinguished 205 m² three-bedroom suite with a private balcony, separate lounge and dining room, kitchen and garden views.
roomTypes.description: Known as the Livingstone Suite, The Victoria Falls Hotel's Presidential Suite is its most expansive accommodation category. Across 205 m², it offers three individually decorated bedrooms, a private balcony with views over the hotel's gardens and generous spaces for relaxing, dining and entertaining. The master bedroom has a spacious bathroom with separate showers and a bathtub. The suite also includes a dedicated kitchen, separate dining room, lounge, dressing space and in-room amenities such as Wi-Fi, minibar, safe, television and air conditioning. Butler service is available by arrangement, allowing guests to tailor the stay to their requirements.
features: Master bathroom with bath & separate showers
Minibar, Wi-Fi, safe, TV & air conditioning

Ideal for couples celebrating special occasions, subject to availability.

roomTypes.name: Presidential Suite

sections.heading: Chapter 1: The Ultimate First-Time Visitor Guide to Victoria Falls

blocks.content: Everything you need to know before planning your trip to Zimbabwe’s most spectacular destination. Published by Outbound Holidays – Victoria Falls Local Travel Specialists.

Planning your first trip to Victoria Falls is exciting—but it can also feel overwhelming. Questions quickly start to pile up: When is the best time to visit? How many days should I stay? Which activities are actually worth it? How much should I budget? Is it safe? Should I stay on the Zimbabwe or Zambia side?

If you’ve been searching online, you’ve probably found dozens of websites giving conflicting advice. Some are outdated. Others are written by people who have only visited once. Many simply list attractions without helping you decide what will actually suit your holiday.

callout.title: 📍 Local Insight: That’s where we do things differently
callout.content: At Outbound Holidays, we’re based in Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe. We spend every day helping travellers from around the world plan memorable holidays here. We know which experiences are worth your time, where to stay based on your travel style, and the little local details that can make all the difference.

blocks.content: This guide brings together everything we’ve learned into one practical resource to help you plan your visit with confidence. Whether you’re travelling as a couple, bringing the family, celebrating a honeymoon, or chasing your next adventure, this guide will help you make informed decisions before you arrive.

Victoria Falls is much more than a waterfall. It’s one of Africa’s most complete travel destinations. Where else can you spend the morning walking through a rainforest beside one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, enjoy lunch overlooking the Batoka Gorge, cruise along the Zambezi River at sunset while watching elephants drink from the riverbank, and finish your evening with traditional Zimbabwean cuisine and live drumming?
That’s what makes Victoria Falls so special. Nature, wildlife, adventure, luxury, culture, and relaxation all come together in one destination.

The waterfall itself—known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, meaning The Smoke That Thunders—is the heart of the experience. During peak water season, more than 500 million litres of water plunge over the edge every minute, creating towering clouds of mist that can be seen from kilometres away.

blocks.content: In our opinion, absolutely. But perhaps not for the reasons you might expect. Many destinations are built around one attraction. Once you’ve seen it, there isn’t much else to do. Victoria Falls is different. The waterfall is the centrepiece, but most visitors are surprised by how much there is to experience beyond it.

sections.heading: Chapter 2: Best Time to Visit Victoria Falls: A Local Month-by-Month Guide

blocks.content: Wondering when to visit Victoria Falls? The answer depends on what you want to experience. Whether you’re hoping to see the Falls at their most powerful, enjoy a sunset cruise on the Zambezi, spot wildlife on safari, or plan a romantic honeymoon, this guide will help you choose the best time for your trip.
One of the first questions we’re asked is: "When is the best time to visit Victoria Falls?" Our answer is always the same: It depends on what kind of holiday you want.

Unlike many destinations, Victoria Falls changes dramatically throughout the year. The volume of water flowing over the Falls rises and falls with the seasons, transforming not only the appearance of the waterfall but also the experiences available to visitors.

practicalPanel.title: Seasons at a Glance
practicalPanel.subtitle: Quick seasonal overview for trip planning

items.heading: March to May (High Water)
items.detail: See the Falls at their most powerful with thunderous flow and lush rainforest spray.

items.heading: August to December (Clear Views)
items.detail: Enjoy crystal-clear views into the gorge, basalt rock formations, and white-water rafting.

items.heading: June to October (Safari Peak)
items.detail: Ideal wildlife viewing conditions as animals congregate around the Zambezi River.

items.heading: May to August (Comfortable Weather)
items.detail: Warm sunny days, crisp cool mornings, low humidity, and excellent sightseeing.

blocks.content: Rather than thinking in terms of four traditional seasons, it’s easier to think of Victoria Falls as having three distinct travel seasons:

This is when the Zambezi River is at its fullest, creating the dramatic spectacle that many people imagine when they think of Victoria Falls. The roar of the water can be heard from kilometres away, and towering clouds of spray give the Falls their local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya—“The Smoke That Thunders.”

Walking through the rainforest during these months is an unforgettable experience. The air is cool with mist, lush vegetation surrounds the pathways, and rainbows often appear throughout the day. However, there is a trade-off: the sheer volume of water and spray can make it difficult to see the entire waterfall from some viewpoints. On windy days, you’ll almost certainly get wet, so a lightweight rain jacket or poncho is highly recommended.

For many travellers, this is the sweet spot. The weather is pleasantly warm during the day, mornings are cool, and rainfall is very unlikely. The spray begins to reduce, revealing more of the cliff face while still showcasing an impressive volume of water. These months are also ideal for combining Victoria Falls with a safari, as wildlife viewing improves in nearby national parks.

callout.title: ⭐ Outbound Recommendation: May Through August
callout.content: If you’re visiting Victoria Falls for the first time and your travel dates are flexible, May through August provides one of the best overall combinations of spectacular waterfall views, pleasant temperatures, and outstanding safari opportunities.

blocks.content: By late winter and into summer, the Zambezi River reaches its lowest levels. Although the waterfall is less dramatic than during peak flow, visitors gain a completely different perspective. The reduced spray allows you to appreciate the immense basalt cliffs and geological formations carved by the river over thousands of years.

This season is also when many of Victoria Falls’ adventure activities are at their best. White-water rafting typically operates under the most favourable river conditions, and visibility throughout the gorge is exceptional. It’s also a fantastic time for wildlife enthusiasts, as animals congregate around remaining water sources in surrounding parks.

callout.title: 📍 Local Insight: Have You Missed the Best Season?
callout.content: Travellers often ask us whether they’ve "missed the best season." The answer is almost always no. Every month offers a different perspective on Victoria Falls. Rather than asking "What’s the best month?", we encourage travellers to ask "What kind of experience do I want?" That’s the question that leads to the right answer.

sections.heading: Chapter 4: Victoria Falls Weather Guide: What to Expect & What to Pack

blocks.content: Planning a trip to Victoria Falls and wondering what the weather will be like? Victoria Falls enjoys a warm subtropical climate, making it a year-round destination. Unlike places that experience harsh winters or extreme seasonal changes, Victoria Falls offers pleasant weather throughout most of the year.

One of the biggest misconceptions about Victoria Falls is that the rainy season means constant rain. Fortunately, that’s rarely the case. Most rainfall arrives in the form of short afternoon thunderstorms. These storms can be dramatic, but they’re often short-lived and usually followed by sunshine.

practicalPanel.subtitle: Essential gear recommended by local travel specialists

items.heading: Year-Round Essentials
items.detail: Comfortable walking shoes, wide-brimmed hat, UV sunglasses, sunscreen, insect repellent, reusable water bottle.

items.heading: Rainy Season (Nov–Apr)
items.detail: Lightweight waterproof jacket or poncho, waterproof dry bags for electronics, quick-drying clothing.

items.heading: Winter Months (Jun–Aug)
items.detail: Light fleece or jacket for cool morning game drives and sunset cruises, long trousers for evenings.

items.heading: Spring Months (Sep–Oct)
items.detail: Breathable cotton/linen clothing, high-SPF sunscreen, electrolyte hydration supplements.

callout.title: 📍 Local Insight: Winter Mornings & Rainforest Spray
callout.content: One of the things that surprises many visitors is just how cool winter mornings can feel on game drives or sunrise cruises. A lightweight jacket takes up very little space in your luggage but makes early starts much more enjoyable. Another surprise is the spray from the Falls themselves—during high water, you will get wetter in the rainforest than during afternoon rain showers!

sections.heading: Chapter 6: Experience Victoria Falls: Our Favourite Experiences

blocks.content: Victoria Falls is one of Africa’s most diverse travel destinations. From witnessing one of the world’s greatest natural wonders to cruising along the Zambezi River at sunset, soaring above the Falls in a helicopter or exploring nearby national parks, there are experiences here for every type of traveller.

The challenge isn’t finding things to do—it’s deciding which experiences are right for you. At Outbound Holidays, we carefully select the experiences we believe offer the greatest value, the most memorable moments, and the best introduction to Victoria Falls.

items: Guided Tour of the Falls (2-3 Hours): Walking through the rainforest with an experienced local guide transforms the Falls from something you simply see into something you truly understand. Learn about geology, history, and cultural significance.

Sunset Cruise on the Zambezi River (2 Hours): Drift past riverbanks where elephants, hippos, crocodiles, and birdlife gather. A peaceful, unhurried way to experience the river as the sun sets over Africa.

Chobe National Park Day Trip (Full Day): Just across the Botswana border, Chobe is famous for its enormous elephant herds. Combines a river safari with a land game drive for spectacular Big 5 sightings.
Game Drive in Victoria Falls Private Reserve (3 Hours): A great introduction to local wildlife, rhino tracking, and buffalo sightings close to town.
Flight of Angels Helicopter Flight (12-25 Mins): Soar high above the Batoka Gorge and Zambezi River for a breathtaking panoramic view of the full waterfall curtain.
White-Water Rafting: World-famous Grade 5 rapids through the Batoka Gorge.
Gorge Swing, Zipline & Bungee Jump: High-adrenaline leaps above the Zambezi gorge.
The Boma – Dinner & Drum Show: An interactive evening of traditional Zimbabwean cuisine, game meats, cultural dancing, and live drumming.

sections.heading: Chapter 9: Getting to Victoria Falls: Everything You Need to Know

blocks.content: Getting to Victoria Falls is easier than many first-time visitors expect. With an international airport, excellent road connections, and convenient regional flights from major Southern African cities, the destination is well connected.

Victoria Falls International Airport (VFA) is located approximately 20 kilometres (12 miles) from the town centre (20-25 minutes by road). Scheduled direct flights connect from Johannesburg, Cape Town, Harare, Nairobi, and Addis Ababa.

callout.title: ⭐ Outbound Flight Recommendation
callout.content: When planning your flights, try to arrive before mid-afternoon if possible. This gives you enough time to settle into your accommodation and enjoy a sunset cruise on your first evening—one of our favourite ways to begin a Victoria Falls holiday.

blocks.content: One question we’re often asked is whether it’s worth staying on the Zimbabwean or Zambian side. For most first-time visitors, we generally recommend staying in Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe. The Zimbabwean side offers 75% of the panoramic viewpoints overlooking the Falls, excellent accommodation options, a lively town centre, and easy access to top experiences.

blocks.content: One of the most common questions we receive is whether you’ll need a visa to visit Zimbabwe. The process is straightforward for most international travellers when you know what to expect before leaving home.

callout.content: If you plan to visit both Zimbabwe and Zambia (or do a day trip to Devil’s Pool or Chobe in Botswana), request the KAZA Univisa ($50 USD) upon arrival at immigration. It grants 30 days of unlimited travel between both countries.

faqs.question: Is Victoria Falls worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Victoria Falls is one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World and one of Africa’s most complete destinations. Beyond the waterfall itself, visitors enjoy wildlife safaris, sunset cruises, helicopter flights, adventure activities, and authentic Zimbabwean hospitality.

faqs.question: How many days should I stay in Victoria Falls?
faqs.answer: For most visitors, we recommend 3 to 4 nights. This gives you enough time to experience the Falls, enjoy a sunset cruise, take part in a safari or adventure activity, and still have time to relax without feeling rushed.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Victoria Falls?
faqs.answer: There isn’t one perfect month—it depends on your priorities! March to May offers peak waterfall flow. May to August is our favourite all-round season for comfortable weather and safaris. June to October is ideal for Big 5 wildlife viewing. August to October is best for white-water rafting.

faqs.question: Is Victoria Falls suitable for families and honeymoons?
faqs.answer: Yes! Victoria Falls effortlessly combines luxury, romance, and family-friendly adventures. Many activities like guided walks, boat cruises, and cultural shows suit children, while luxury lodges and private cruises offer incredible romantic getaways.

faqs.question: Which currency is used in Victoria Falls?
faqs.answer: The US Dollar (USD) is the most widely accepted currency in Victoria Falls. Visa and Mastercard are accepted at most hotels, restaurants, and activity operators, but carrying cash USD in small denominations ($1, $5, $10, $20) is recommended for tipping, local craft markets, and taxi fares.

faqs.question: Are credit cards accepted and how much cash should I bring?
faqs.answer: Major credit cards (Visa and Mastercard) are accepted at almost all hotels, established restaurants, and safari operators. However, ATMs can occasionally run out of cash or experience connectivity issues. We advise bringing around $200–$300 in small USD cash notes per person for incidental expenses, park fees, tips, and market shopping.

faqs.question: What are the must-do experiences for first-timers?
faqs.answer: If it’s your first visit, we recommend: 1) Guided Tour of Victoria Falls rainforest, 2) Zambezi Sunset Cruise, 3) Flight of Angels Helicopter Flight over the gorge, 4) Chobe National Park Day Trip or local Zambezi National Park Game Drive, and 5) The Boma Dinner & Drum Show.

faqs.question: Can I visit both Zimbabwe and Zambia during my stay?
faqs.answer: Yes! You can cross the Victoria Falls Bridge between both countries easily. Obtaining the KAZA Univisa ($50 USD) on arrival at immigration allows unlimited cross-border travel between Zimbabwe and Zambia for up to 30 days.

faqs.question: Is Victoria Falls safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Victoria Falls is widely considered one of Southern Africa’s safest tourist destinations. The town is compact, welcoming, peaceful, and easy to navigate. Dedicated tourist police and local guides ensure visitors feel safe day and night.

faqs.question: Do I need malaria medication and is tap water safe?
faqs.answer: Victoria Falls is situated in a low-risk malaria zone, so we recommend consulting your doctor or travel clinic before departing for recommended prophylaxis. Most hotels provide filtered or bottled drinking water, which we recommend using during your stay for drinking and brushing teeth.

faqs.question: What is the weather like and what should I pack for Victoria Falls?
faqs.answer: Victoria Falls enjoys a warm climate year-round. Summer (November to March) is warm to hot with occasional afternoon rain showers. Winter (May to August) brings clear sunny days (20°C–25°C) and cool evenings (8°C–12°C). Pack lightweight breathable clothing, comfortable walking shoes, a waterproof jacket or raincoat for the rainforest spray, sun protection (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen), and warm layers for early morning safaris and winter evenings.

faqs.question: Will I get wet when viewing Victoria Falls?
faqs.answer: During peak flow months (March to July), you will experience heavy spray and rain-like mist in the rainforest national park. You will definitely get soaked on certain viewpoints, which is part of the exhilarating experience! Ponchos and waterproof phone cases can be rented at the entrance or provided by your guide.

faqs.question: Will I see elephants and the Big Five?
faqs.answer: Elephants are frequently seen along the Zambezi River and in surrounding national parks. Local game drives in Zambezi National Park offer sightings of lions, buffalo, giraffes, zebras, and antelopes. For guaranteed Big Five viewing, a day trip to Chobe National Park in Botswana or a multi-day safari extension to Hwange National Park is highly recommended.

faqs.question: Where should I stay in Victoria Falls (Boutique Lodges vs Town Hotels)?
faqs.answer: Choosing accommodation depends on your preference: 1) Riverside Boutique Lodges offer serene luxury, direct Zambezi river views, and inclusive dining, 2) Town Hotels offer convenient walking access to local markets, cafes, and the Falls rainforest, and 3) Safari Camps inside national parks offer immersive bush stays.

faqs.question: Why should I book through Outbound Holidays?
faqs.answer: We don’t believe in one-size-fits-all templates. Based directly in Victoria Falls, our local specialists carefully curate your accommodation, transfers, and activities around your specific budget and travel style with 24/7 on-ground concierge support and zero hidden fees.

faqs.question: How far in advance should I book my Victoria Falls trip?
faqs.answer: For peak travel months (June to October) and festive holiday periods, we recommend booking 4 to 6 months in advance to secure preferred boutique lodges, private safari vehicles, and prime flight slots. However, our local team can also arrange seamless last-minute itineraries.

sections.heading: When Is the Best Time to Visit Victoria Falls?

blocks.content: Wondering when to visit Victoria Falls? The answer depends on what you want to experience. Whether you’re hoping to see the Falls at their most powerful, enjoy a sunset cruise on the Zambezi, spot wildlife on safari, or plan a romantic honeymoon, this guide will help you choose the best time for your trip.
One of the first questions we’re asked is: "When is the best time to visit Victoria Falls?" Our answer is always the same: It depends on what kind of holiday you want.

Unlike many destinations, Victoria Falls changes dramatically throughout the year. The volume of water flowing over the Falls rises and falls with the seasons, transforming not only the appearance of the waterfall but also the experiences available to visitors.

During some months, you’ll witness immense walls of water crashing into the gorge, sending mist hundreds of metres into the air. At other times, the spray clears to reveal the full basalt cliff face, making it easier to appreciate the incredible scale of the Falls and opening up seasonal adventures like white-water rafting.

sections.heading: Understanding the Three Travel Seasons

blocks.content: This is when the Zambezi River is at its fullest, creating the dramatic spectacle that many people imagine when they think of Victoria Falls. The roar of the water can be heard from kilometres away, and towering clouds of spray give the Falls their local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya—“The Smoke That Thunders.”

Walking through the rainforest during these months is an unforgettable experience. The air is cool with mist, lush vegetation surrounds the pathways, and rainbows often appear throughout the day. However, there is a trade-off: the sheer volume of water and spray can make it difficult to see the entire waterfall from some viewpoints. On windy days, you’ll almost certainly get wet, so a lightweight rain jacket or poncho is highly recommended.

items: Best for first-time visitors wanting maximum flow spectacle
Photographers looking for towering mist and vivid rainbows
Nature lovers appreciating the lush rainforest environment
Scenic Flight of Angels helicopter flights

blocks.content: For many travellers, this is the sweet spot. The weather is pleasantly warm during the day, mornings are cool, and rainfall is very unlikely. The spray begins to reduce, revealing more of the cliff face while still showcasing an impressive volume of water. These months are also ideal for combining Victoria Falls with a safari, as wildlife viewing improves in nearby national parks.

callout.title: ⭐ Outbound Recommendation: May Through August
callout.content: If you’re visiting Victoria Falls for the first time and your travel dates are flexible, May through August provides one of the best overall combinations of spectacular waterfall views, pleasant temperatures, and outstanding safari opportunities.

blocks.content: By late winter and into summer, the Zambezi River reaches its lowest levels. Although the waterfall is less dramatic than during peak flow, visitors gain a completely different perspective. The reduced spray allows you to appreciate the immense basalt cliffs and geological formations carved by the river over thousands of years.

This season is also when many of Victoria Falls’ adventure activities are at their best. White-water rafting typically operates under the most favourable river conditions, and visibility throughout the gorge is exceptional. It’s also a fantastic time for wildlife enthusiasts, as animals congregate around remaining water sources in surrounding parks.

sections.heading: Which Season Do We Recommend?

items: Choose March to May if... You want to experience the Falls at their most powerful and don’t mind getting a little wet. This is the most dramatic time of year, with thunderous water, lush rainforest, and spectacular rainbows.

Choose May to August if... You want the best all-round holiday. Comfortable temperatures, impressive waterfall views, excellent safari conditions, and a full range of activities make this our favourite period for first-time visitors.

Choose September to October if... Adventure activities and wildlife are your priority. The Falls are easier to view, rafting conditions are excellent, and animals are easier to spot in nearby national parks.

Choose November to January if... You’re looking for fewer visitors, greener landscapes, and don’t mind occasional afternoon showers. The rainy season begins to transform the landscape, creating a fresh and vibrant environment.

callout.title: 📍 Local Insight: Have You Missed the Best Season?
callout.content: Travellers often ask us whether they’ve "missed the best season." The answer is almost always no. Every month offers a different perspective on Victoria Falls. Some visitors are captivated by the thunderous power of high water, while others fall in love with crystal-clear views and dramatic gorge scenery during low water. Rather than asking "What’s the best month?", we encourage travellers to ask "What kind of experience do I want?" That’s the question that leads to the right answer.

sections.heading: What’s the Weather Like in Victoria Falls?

blocks.content: Victoria Falls enjoys a warm subtropical climate, making it a year-round destination. Unlike places that experience harsh winters or extreme seasonal changes, Victoria Falls offers pleasant weather throughout most of the year.

That said, the climate changes noticeably between the rainy and dry seasons. These changes influence not only the temperature but also the appearance of the Falls, wildlife viewing, and the types of experiences available.

table.title: Average Temperature & Rainfall Throughout the Year

blocks.content: One of the biggest misconceptions about Victoria Falls is that the rainy season means constant rain. Fortunately, that’s rarely the case. Most rainfall arrives in the form of short afternoon thunderstorms. These storms can be dramatic, but they’re often short-lived and usually followed by sunshine.

Morning activities generally continue as planned, and many visitors find the storms add to the atmosphere rather than detract from it. The rain also brings cooler temperatures and transforms the surrounding landscape into a lush, green paradise.

sections.heading: Our Recommended Experiences, Carefully Chosen by Local Specialists

blocks.content: Victoria Falls is one of Africa’s most diverse travel destinations. From witnessing one of the world’s greatest natural wonders to cruising along the Zambezi River at sunset, soaring above the Falls in a helicopter or exploring nearby national parks, there are experiences here for every type of traveller.

The challenge isn’t finding things to do—it’s deciding which experiences are right for you. At Outbound Holidays, we don’t believe in recommending every activity available. Instead, we’ve carefully selected the experiences we believe offer the greatest value, the most memorable moments, and the best introduction to Victoria Falls.

sections.heading: Top Experiences by Category

items: Guided Tour of the Falls (2–3 Hours): Walking through the rainforest with an experienced guide transforms the Falls from something you simply see into something you truly understand. Perfect for everyone.
Sunset Cruise on the Zambezi River (2 Hours): Drift past islands and riverbanks where elephants, hippos, crocodiles, and birdlife gather. Perfect for couples, families, and first-timers.
Chobe National Park Day Trip (Full Day): Just across the border in Botswana, famous for enormous elephant herds, land game drives, and river safaris.
Game Drive in Victoria Falls Area (3 Hours): Great introduction to local African wildlife, rhino tracking, and buffalo sightings.
Flight of Angels Helicopter Flight (12–15 Mins): Unforgettable aerial view of the full waterfall width and Batoka Gorge.
White Water Rafting: World-class Grade 5 rafting through Batoka Gorge rapids.
Gorge Swing, Zipline & Bungee Jumping: Adrenaline-packed leaps high above the Zambezi River.
The Boma – Dinner & Drum Show: Traditional Zimbabwean cuisine, game meats, cultural dancing, and live interactive drumming.
Gorge & Riverside Dining: Lookout Café, Baines Restaurant, Three Monkeys, and Palm River Restaurant.

callout.title: 📍 Local Insight: The 3-Day Priority Formula
callout.content: If you only have three days, our local specialists recommend prioritizing: 1) Guided Tour of the Falls, 2) Sunset Cruise, 3) One wildlife experience (Game Drive or Chobe Day Trip), and 4) One special experience (Helicopter Flight or Boma Dinner). These four experiences provide a wonderful introduction without making your itinerary feel rushed.

callout.title: ⭐ Outbound Activity Recommendation
callout.content: You don’t need to experience everything Victoria Falls has to offer to have an unforgettable holiday. The best trips aren’t the ones packed with the most activities—they’re the ones where each experience feels meaningful and well-paced.

sections.heading: Where is Victoria Falls & How Do You Fly In?

blocks.content: Getting to Victoria Falls is easier than many first-time visitors expect. With an international airport, excellent road connections, and convenient regional flights from major Southern African cities, the destination is well connected for travellers from around the world.

Victoria Falls is located in north-western Zimbabwe, on the banks of the mighty Zambezi River, where Zimbabwe meets Zambia. The town is home to Victoria Falls International Airport (VFA) and sits just a few minutes from the entrance to Victoria Falls National Park.

items: Johannesburg (JNB): Multiple daily direct flights (1.5 hours)
Cape Town (CPT): Direct scheduled flights (2.5 hours)
Harare (HRE): Daily domestic flights (1 hour)
Nairobi (NBO) & Addis Ababa (ADD): Regional direct connections

callout.title: ⭐ Outbound Flight Recommendation
callout.content: When planning your flights, try to arrive before mid-afternoon if possible. This gives you enough time to settle into your accommodation and enjoy a sunset cruise on your first evening—one of our favourite ways to begin a Victoria Falls holiday.

sections.heading: Airport Transfers & Regional Combinations

blocks.content: Victoria Falls International Airport is located approximately 20 kilometres (12 miles) from the town centre. The journey to most hotels takes around 20–25 minutes by road. Pre-booking an airport transfer ensures a driver is waiting upon arrival, removing stress after a long flight.

blocks.subheading: Combining Victoria Falls with Other Destinations

items: Victoria Falls + Hwange National Park (Zimbabwe): Classic waterfall & Big 5 safari combo.
Victoria Falls + Chobe National Park (Botswana): Famous elephant herds and river safaris.
Victoria Falls + Cape Town (South Africa): Natural wonder meets vibrant coastal city life.
Victoria Falls + Okavango Delta (Botswana): Ultimate luxury African safari combination.

callout.title: 📍 Local Insight: Zimbabwe vs. Zambia Side Selection
callout.content: One question we’re often asked is whether it’s worth staying on the Zimbabwean or Zambian side. For most first-time visitors, we generally recommend staying in Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe. The Zimbabwean side offers 75% of the panoramic viewpoints overlooking the Falls, excellent accommodation options, a lively town centre, and easy access to top experiences.

sections.heading: Passport Requirements & Visa Categories

blocks.content: One of the most common questions we receive is whether you’ll need a visa to visit Zimbabwe. The good news is that the process is straightforward for most international travellers, especially when you know what to expect before you leave home.

items: Passport Validity: Valid for at least 6 months beyond date of arrival.
Blank Pages: At least two blank pages for immigration stamps.
Physical Condition: In good condition without significant damage.
Category A (Visa-Free Entry): Eligible nationalities proceed directly through immigration.
Category B (Visa on Arrival): UK, US, Australia, Germany, France, Netherlands, Italy, Japan, Canada, and many others obtain visas at airport immigration.
Category C (Visa Required Before Travel): Requires advance application prior to departure.

blocks.content: If you’re planning to visit both Zimbabwe and Zambia, you may be eligible for the KAZA Univisa ($50 USD), which allows travel between both countries without purchasing separate visas. This is an excellent option if your itinerary includes viewing the Falls from both sides, Devil’s Pool, or day trips into Livingstone.

callout.title: 📍 Local Tip: Online Declaration Form
callout.content: Complete your online Zimbabwe Immigration Declaration before leaving home rather than relying on airport Wi-Fi after landing. It makes your arrival much quicker and less stressful.

strings.travel/AboutPage.text18: I’m Fungai Mtetwa, the travel advisor behind Outbound Holidays. Victoria Falls is home, and I’ve spent more than nine years working in tourism here.

strings.travel/AboutPage.text20: My job is to make those decisions easier. I personally help you understand your options and put together a holiday that suits your budget, interests, pace and the people you’re travelling with.
strings.travel/AboutPage.text21: That starts with listening. A family holiday, a couple’s getaway and a first safari need different things, and I want to understand yours before recommending anything.

strings.travel/AboutPage.text25: I started Outbound Holidays to help bridge that gap. I bring local knowledge and personal guidance to those choices, then help accommodation, activities and transfers fit together without rushing your holiday or spending unnecessarily.

strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text1: What time does The Boma start and end?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text2: The Boma evening begins at 6:45 PM with a ceremonial traditional welcome, hand washing, and village beer tasting. The interactive drumming show reaches its crescendo around 8:45 PM, followed by table acapella serenades and desserts. The evening concludes between 9:45 PM and 10:00 PM.
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text3: Is hotel transfer included in the experience?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text4: Round-trip hotel transfers are optional and can be arranged with your quotation. The Boma operates daily from 19:00 to 22:00 at the Victoria Falls Safari Lodge estate.
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text5: What food is served at the African buffet?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text6: The evening begins with a waiter-served starter platter including smoked crocodile tail, salted groundnuts with 'Nyimo' round nuts, and corn fritters. The main buffet features an open-fire braai with grilled game meats, beef, pork, chicken, and daily spit roast, plus traditional 'Umzingeli' hunter's potjie stews, Zambezi bream, Kapenta whitebait, peanut butter rice, and authentic sadza (isitshwala).
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text7: Are vegetarian and vegan options available?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text8: Yes! The Boma caters generously to vegetarian and plant-based diners with dedicated cooking stations preparing daily chef's pasta, vegetable stir-fries, bush vegetables, fresh soups, oven-baked garlic bread, and an extensive fresh salad bar including three-bean salad, sweet potato salad, potato salad, and beetroot salad.

strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text11: What should I wear to The Boma?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text12: Dress code is smart casual and comfortable. The dining area is thatched and partially open-air under the African night sky, so a light sweater or jacket is recommended during winter months (May to August).
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text13: How long does the evening last?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text14: The full experience lasts approximately 3 hours (6:45 PM to 10:00 PM), allowing ample time to savour all four courses, enjoy the live traditional dancers, participate in the interactive drumming, and relax with tea, coffee, or dessert.
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text15: Should I book The Boma in advance?
strings.travel/BomaExperiencePage.text16: Yes, advance reservations are strongly recommended. As Victoria Falls' flagship cultural dining experience, seats sell out quickly—especially during high safari season (July through October) and festive holiday periods.

strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text12: Leap forward into pure weightlessness! Experience 4 seconds of exhilarating freefall reaching terminal speeds over 120 km/h before the custom rubber bungee cord smoothly catches you in a series of gentle, soaring bounces.
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text15: After the rebounds settle, a winch operator lowers a recovery line to hoist you smoothly back up to the bridge deck, where optional photo and video footage can be viewed.
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text16: Is a visa required to go onto the Victoria Falls Bridge?
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text17: A physical passport is required to access the Victoria Falls Bridge. Visa and border-crossing requirements depend on your nationality and itinerary—our team will advise before booking.
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text18: How safe is the Victoria Falls Bungee Jump?
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text19: It is operated under strict British & Australian bungee standards with dual-redundant harness systems, daily cord inspections, and a 100% safety record across more than 500,000 jumps since 1994.
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text20: Can non-jumping family and friends watch from the bridge?
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text21: Absolutely! Spectating from the bridge walkways or enjoying a cold beverage at the Bridge Café is completely free and provides an incredible vantage point for photos and videos.
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text22: What are the age and weight requirements?
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text23: Minimum age is 14 years. Shearwater bungee terms specify a minimum weight of 40 kg (88 lbs) and maximum weight of 120 kg (265 lbs). Parents or legal guardians must sign consent for jumpers under 18.
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text24: What should I wear for the bungee jump?
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text25: Wear comfortable clothing and closed-toe footwear like sneakers or running shoes. Loose objects, glasses, and pocket items must be secured or left in lockers at the jump office.

strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text43: "The Victoria Falls Bridge bungee isn't just a jump; it's a plunge into the natural border between Zimbabwe and Zambia with one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World roaring right beside you. The sheer drop, the wind, and the mist create an adrenaline rush unmatched anywhere in Africa."
strings.travel/BungeeExperiencePage.text44: Spanning the canyon between two countries, the historic 1905 Victoria Falls Railway Bridge offers a leaping platform unlike any other on earth. As you stand on the jump gantry 111 meters above the churning white water of the Zambezi River, the roaring mist of Mosi-oa-Tunya forms giant rainbows across the basalt cliffs. It is equal parts awe-inspiring engineering, raw nature, and extreme bucket-list adventure.

strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text2: The experiences we recommend before anything else on a first visit to Victoria Falls.

strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text14: Holistic botanical massages, plunge pools and rejuvenating safari wellness overlooking the bush.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text15: Which experiences should a first-time visitor prioritise?
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text16: For first-time visitors, we strongly recommend starting with a Guided Tour of Victoria Falls rainforest, an Upper Zambezi Sunset Cruise, and the iconic Boma Dinner Experience. If time allows, adding the Flight of Angels helicopter tour provides an extraordinary aerial perspective.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text17: How far in advance should I book activities?
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text18: We recommend booking popular experiences—such as helicopter flights, sunset cruises, and Chobe day safaris—at least 2 to 4 weeks in advance during peak season (June to October) to guarantee preferred time slots.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text19: Can experiences be combined into one itinerary?
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text20: Absolutely! Most activities can be seamlessly scheduled across 2 to 4 days. Our local specialists ensure ideal timing so you enjoy relaxed transitions between morning tours, afternoon safaris, and evening dining.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text22: Yes, almost all guided experiences in Victoria Falls town include return hotel transfers from major lodges and hotels.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text24: Many activities—including rainforest tours, sunset cruises, cultural Boma dinners, and family safaris—are fantastic for all ages. Age restrictions apply only to extreme adrenaline adventures like bungee jumping or white-water rafting.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text26: Activity costs cover guided services and transport, while government park entry fees ($50 international per person for rainforest entry) are paid directly at park gates unless specified in your custom package.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text27: Can Outbound Holidays recommend experiences based on my budget?
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text28: Yes! Our local advisors design custom experience bundles tailored precisely to your budget, travel dates, and preferred pace.
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text29: What happens if weather affects an activity?
strings.travel/ExperiencesDirectoryPage.text30: Your safety is our priority. If an activity like a helicopter flight is postponed due to weather, we will rebook it for another time during your stay or issue a full refund.

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: The Boma evening begins at 6:45 PM with a ceremonial traditional welcome, hand washing, and village beer tasting. The interactive drumming show reaches its crescendo around 8:45 PM, followed by table acapella serenades and desserts. The evening concludes between 9:45 PM and 10:00 PM.
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: What time does The Boma start and end?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: Round-trip hotel transfers are optional and can be easily bundled with your reservation. Our air-conditioned vehicles pick you up directly from your Victoria Falls hotel or safari lodge around 6:15 PM and return you safely after the show.
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: Is hotel transfer included in the experience?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: The evening begins with a waiter-served starter platter including smoked crocodile tail, salted groundnuts with 'Nyimo' round nuts, and corn fritters. The main buffet features an open-fire braai with grilled game meats, beef, pork, chicken, and daily spit roast, plus traditional 'Umzingeli' hunter's potjie stews, Zambezi bream, Kapenta whitebait, peanut butter rice, and authentic sadza (isitshwala).
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: What food is served at the African buffet?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: Yes! The Boma caters generously to vegetarian and plant-based diners with dedicated cooking stations preparing daily chef's pasta, vegetable stir-fries, bush vegetables, fresh soups, oven-baked garlic bread, and an extensive fresh salad bar including three-bean salad, sweet potato salad, potato salad, and beetroot salad.
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: Are vegetarian and vegan options available?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: Extremely family-friendly! Children of all ages love the vibrant energy, face painting, interactive drumming session where every guest gets their own Djembe drum, and the fun 'mopane worm' tasting challenge (with an official certificate for those brave enough to try!).
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: Is The Boma family-friendly for children?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: Dress code is smart casual and comfortable. The dining area is thatched and partially open-air under the African night sky, so a light sweater or jacket is recommended during winter months (May to August).
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: What should I wear to The Boma?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: The full experience lasts approximately 3 hours (6:45 PM to 10:00 PM), allowing ample time to savour all four courses, enjoy the live traditional dancers, participate in the interactive drumming, and relax with tea, coffee, or dessert.
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: How long does the evening last?

travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.a: Yes, advance reservations are strongly recommended. As Victoria Falls' flagship cultural dining experience, seats sell out quickly—especially during high safari season (July through October) and festive holiday periods.
travel/BomaExperiencePage.section1.q: Should I book The Boma in advance?

travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.title: The Historic Bridge Approach
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.highlight: Free bridge pass provided at border control—no visa needed!
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.description: Walk out onto the famous 1905 steel Victoria Falls Railway Bridge spanning the Batoka Gorge. Positioned in the neutral 'No-Man's Land' between Zimbabwe and Zambia, you'll feel the rush of wind and catch your first glimpse of the roaring river 111 meters below.

travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.title: Safety Briefing & Precision Harnessing
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.highlight: Operated with a 100% safety record over 500,000+ jumps.
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.description: Meet your team of certified master riggers at the bridge jump station. You will be weighed, fitted with specialized padded ankle harnesses, and backed up with a heavy-duty climbing body harness for dual-redundant safety.

travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.title: The Edge Walk & Gantry Launchpad
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.highlight: Breathtaking 360° panoramic view of Batoka Canyon.
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.description: Step onto the wooden jump gantry suspended directly over the abyss. With the spray of Mosi-oa-Tunya drifting past and the Zambezi rapids surging under your feet, the jump master guides you to the threshold.

travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.title: 5... 4... 3... 2... 1... BUNGEE!
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.highlight: 4 seconds of sheer vertical zero-gravity freefall.
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.description: Leap forward into pure weightlessness! Experience 4 seconds of exhilarating freefall reaching terminal speeds over 120 km/h before the custom rubber bungee cord smoothly catches you in a series of gentle, soaring bounces.

travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.title: Winch Recovery & Certificate of Bravery
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.highlight: Official Certificate of Bravery & HD video memories.
travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section1.description: After the rebounds settle, a winch operator gently lowers a recovery line to hoist you smoothly back up to the bridge deck. Celebrate with fellow jumpers, receive your official Certificate of Bravery, and view your HD video footage.

travel/BungeeExperiencePage.section2.a: No! Border control at both the Zimbabwean and Zambian posts issue a complimentary Bridge Pass so you can step onto the bridge without using up a visa entry or paying border entry fees.

VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.name: Victoria Falls Rainforest Park
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.fullDesc: A lush micro-rainforest nourished perpetually by the spray of the Falls. Walk along paved paths to legendary viewpoints including Danger Point, Cataract Island, and the Main Falls.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.shortDesc: Walk along the precipice of Mosi-oa-Tunya with 16 panoramic viewpoints.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.insiderTip: Visit between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM to see brilliant double rainbows arches across the gorge!

VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.name: Zambezi River Sunset Cruise
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.fullDesc: Cruising the upper Zambezi River above the Falls is an iconic Zimbabwean ritual. Watch hippos emerge, fish eagles soar, and elephants swim between islands as the sunset paints the sky in deep amber.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.shortDesc: Glide along calm river waters while elephants cross and hippos wallow.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.insiderTip: Ask for a seat on the top deck for unobstructed 360-degree photography views.

VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.name: The Lookout Café
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.fullDesc: Enjoy artisan cocktails, grilled impala, and craft coffee while sitting right over the edge of Batoka Gorge, watching thrill-seekers gorge swing and zipline in front of your eyes.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.shortDesc: Cliffside dining perched 120m directly above the Batoka Gorge rapids.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.insiderTip: Book a table for 4:30 PM to secure prime cliffside sunset seating.

VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.name: Batoka Gorge Swing & Zipline
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.fullDesc: For adrenaline seekers, leap off the edge into a breathtaking freefall before swinging high across the river gorge with views of the historic Victoria Falls Bridge.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.shortDesc: A heart-pounding 70m freefall into the spectacular gorge.
VIC_FALLS_SPOTS.insiderTip: Tandem swings are available for couples or parents jumping with teens!
